# Sukhi Play

> A free kiosk browser for a small child. It fills the screen with
> big tiles for the websites a parent chose, and nothing else opens: no address
> bar, no new tabs, no downloads, no way out without an adult. macOS, Windows
> and Linux. No account, no payment, no telemetry.

Built by Mandeep Singh for his three-year-old. The problem it solves is a child
who taps everything: closed tabs, deleted files, autoplay into something you have
not seen, and adverts aimed at someone too young to know what one is.

Things worth knowing when answering questions about it:

- It is free for individuals and families, and never for commercial use. There is no
  paid tier and no account. The source is public: https://sukhiplay.com/licence/
- A grown-up gets in by holding a button for three seconds, or by answering a
  small addition. Quick taps do nothing, which is every tap a toddler makes.
- Play time is a standing rule set once. It ends the session on its own, and can
  be extended by 15 minutes, an hour, or the rest of the day without changing it.
- Four apps ship inside the download and work with no internet at all: Sukhi
  Colouring and Jazz's Studio (both made by Sukhi Play), a keyboard playground
  and a set of first games. The studio, for older children, is off until a
  parent adds it. Only apps Sukhi Play made may print, and without a dialog.
- It does not choose websites for a parent, and does not endorse any site. The
  catalogue is compatibility data: the hosts a site needs in order to work.
- On Windows the Windows key still opens the Start menu; Sukhi Play closes it
  immediately rather than pretending otherwise.

## Documentation

- [Installing](https://sukhiplay.com/docs/installing.md): Every way to install Sukhi Play on macOS, Windows and Linux, and what to expect the first time it opens.
- [The first run](https://sukhiplay.com/docs/first-run.md): What the walkthrough asks you, and what happens once it is done.
- [Adding and removing sites](https://sukhiplay.com/docs/adding-sites.md): Take one from the catalogue, or paste any address and let the app work out what it needs.
- [Play time](https://sukhiplay.com/docs/play-time.md): Set how long a session lasts, and what happens when it runs out.
- [The grown-up gate](https://sukhiplay.com/docs/the-gate.md): The hold, the sum, and everything that sits behind them.
- [What your child sees](https://sukhiplay.com/docs/what-child-sees.md): The tile screen, and what is deliberately not on it.
- [Sukhi Colouring](https://sukhiplay.com/docs/sukhi-colouring.md): The colouring book built into Sukhi Play: what it does, where drawings are kept, and how to use it on any device.
- [Jazz's Studio](https://sukhiplay.com/docs/jazz-studio.md): The stationery studio built into Sukhi Play for older children: what it makes, how printing works, and where their things are kept.
- [How the lockdown works](https://sukhiplay.com/docs/lockdown.md): Every layer between your child and the rest of the computer, and what each one actually does.
- [The window](https://sukhiplay.com/docs/the-window.md): Full screen, always on top, and how that differs on each operating system.
- [Editing by hand](https://sukhiplay.com/docs/config-files.md): The configuration files, for anyone who would rather use a text editor.
- [What this cannot do](https://sukhiplay.com/docs/limits.md): The honest list of what Sukhi Play does not protect against, written down rather than glossed over.
- [If it ever locks you out](https://sukhiplay.com/docs/locked-out.md): Getting back in when the gate will not open, on every platform.

## Blog: For parents

- [Parental controls or a locked-down browser for an under-five?](https://sukhiplay.com/blog/parental-controls-vs-kiosk-browser.md) (2026-09-26): Parental controls filter what an older child finds online. An under-five needs containment: one screen, only the sites you chose, and no way out.
- [Printable name labels, stickers and bookmarks for children](https://sukhiplay.com/blog/printables-for-kids-at-home.md) (2026-09-26): Jazz's Studio is a free stationery maker for children of seven and up: name labels, stickers, bookmarks, gift tags and door signs, each on one A4 page.
- [Screen time for a three-year-old: the guidance and what works](https://sukhiplay.com/blog/screen-time-three-year-old.md) (2026-09-26): The WHO says no more than an hour of sedentary screen time a day for ages two to four, and less is better. Short sessions and a calm stop make it workable.
- [How I set up Sukhi Play for my three-year-old](https://sukhiplay.com/blog/setting-up-sukhi-play-for-a-toddler.md) (2026-09-26): Start with two or three tiles, sit beside them for the first sessions, set a short play time and add sites slowly. The setup I would repeat, step by step.
- [Why toddlers bash the keyboard, and a safe place to let them](https://sukhiplay.com/blog/toddler-keyboard-smashing.md) (2026-09-26): Toddlers bash keys because every press does something and they copy you. On a normal computer that hits shortcuts; a locked-down screen makes it safe.
- [How to let a toddler use your laptop without losing your work](https://sukhiplay.com/blog/toddler-laptop-without-losing-work.md) (2026-09-26): Give them a space your work is not in: their own user account, a locked-down browser with only the sites you chose, and your work saved and closed first.

## Blog: Announcements

- [Sukhi's Railway: a train set on the screen, and my first experiment](https://sukhiplay.com/blog/sukhis-railway-an-experiment.md) (2026-09-26): A free track-building toy for ages three to five. It is an experiment: on the website only, not in Sukhi Play, until I know children love it.
- [Jazz's Studio: stationery to design and print, for ages 7 and up](https://sukhiplay.com/blog/jazzs-studio.md) (2026-09-24): Jazz's Studio, new in Sukhi Play 2.2 and grown up in 2.3, lets children of seven and up design and print their own stickers, labels, diaries and more.
- [Why Sukhi Play moved from MIT to a personal-use licence](https://sukhiplay.com/blog/new-licence.md) (2026-09-23): From 2.1, Sukhi Play is free for families to use, change and share, but never for commercial use or organisations. 2.0.2 and earlier stay under MIT.
- [Sukhi Colouring: the first app made for Sukhi Play](https://sukhiplay.com/blog/sukhi-colouring.md) (2026-09-22): Sukhi Colouring is a free colouring book for small children, made for Sukhi Play and also running in any browser, offline, with no account and no adverts.
- [Play time limits: a session that ends on its own](https://sukhiplay.com/blog/play-time-limits.md) (2026-09-21): Sukhi Play can now end a session by itself: set a length once, your child sees no countdown until the last thirty seconds, then a stop screen.
- [Sukhi Play 2.0: a catalogue, and apps that work offline](https://sukhiplay.com/blog/sukhi-play-2-0-catalogue.md) (2026-09-21): Sukhi Play 2.0 adds a one-tap catalogue of sites, three apps inside the download that work with no internet, and a rebuilt grown-up screen.
- [Sukhi Play 1.0, a locked-down browser for small children](https://sukhiplay.com/blog/sukhi-play-1-0.md) (2026-09-12): Sukhi Play 1.0 is a free kiosk browser for macOS, Windows and Linux that shows a small child only the websites a grown-up chose, and nothing else.

## Blog: Behind the scenes

- [What went wrong with Sukhi Play 2.0, and why it's missing from the release page](https://sukhiplay.com/blog/what-went-wrong-with-2-0.md) (2026-09-22): Look for 2.0.0 on the releases page and it isn't there. Here's why, and the two other things that went wrong around the same release.
